text:
There's no single best combo. It depends on what you run and how long you stay off-grid. I couldn't open retailer pages, so most links below go to the review pages I used, where each source has its own buy buttons. Check current prices there.

## Pick by RV use

**Weekend trips (fridge, Starlink, laptops, CPAP): about 1,000Wh**
- **EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus** was ranked best overall for camping. It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output and about 28 lb of weight. It accepts up to 1,000W of solar through two 500W inputs and expands to 5kWh. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2** is the simpler, lighter option (1,070Wh, 23.8 lb). Its solar input is capped at 400W, so two 200W SolarSaga panels is the right size and more won't help. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Longer boondocking, 30A hookup (about 2,000Wh)**
- **BLUETTI AC200L** has 2,048Wh, 2,400W, a built-in 30A RV outlet and up to 1,200W of solar input. It's the value pick. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/))

**Running a roof A/C or full-timing**
- **EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3** has 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge, and expands past 12kWh. It was the top RV pick, but it's heavy and costs the most. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro** has 3,000W continuous and 6,000W surge, which is enough to start a 13,500 BTU A/C. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **ALLPOWERS R4000** has 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, an RV outlet and up to 2,000W of solar input. It was listed at $1,499, or $1,319.12 with code EXTRA12 when tested on 2026-10-23. It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb). Reaching 2,000W of solar needs panels on all three inputs. [Buy at ALLPOWERS via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (affiliate link). ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

## Panels
- NomadSignal suggests the Renogy 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase or a 100W foldable panel. ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife))
- Jackery SolarSaga 100W and 200W panels pair with the Explorer line, and EcoFlow sells its own panels for the DELTA series.
- Check the station's maximum solar input before buying panels. A big array can be bottlenecked by a low input limit. ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life))

## Caveats
- Nearly all of these sources earn affiliate commissions. Their specs agree with each other, but treat the rankings as opinion.
- One source reports the older Bluetti AC200P at a 700W solar cap, while the newer AC200L is listed at 1,200W. Confirm the exact model.
- The EmergencyEnergy article is written for Ontario, Canada, so ignore its electrical-code advice. Have a licensed electrician do any hardwired RV connection.

If you tell me your RV type, your main loads (A/C, fridge, CPAP, Starlink) and your budget, I can narrow this to one station and a matching panel setup.
